title: Push Notifications With ntfy
bottom_line: Ask Claude to notify you, or run /ntfy:ntfy. It sends a push to your ntfy topic, reaching every phone, desktop or browser subscribed.

sections.heading: Ask in plain words, or call the skill by name

blocks.caption: The skill takes no argument. You can also just ask, as below.

blocks.title: From a sentence to a push

nodes.label: You ask in chat
nodes.note: "Ping me on ntfy when this build finishes"

nodes.label: Notification sent
nodes.note: To your server and topic, with title, priority and tags as needed.

blocks.title: Phrases that trigger it
items: "Ping me on ntfy when this build finishes"
"Send me a push notification if the tests fail, topic `ci-alerts`"

blocks.text: It lets Claude ping you when a long-running task finishes, a build fails, or anything else worth interrupting you for. Other plugins in this marketplace use it too: `plan-tools` (`drain-issues`) and `compliance-audit` (`apply`) send their "finished" and "stuck" alerts through it.

terms.definition: An HTTP pub-sub notification service. A message posted to <server>/<topic> reaches every subscriber to that topic. No accounts, no SDKs, plain HTTP.
The channel name notifications go to. Anyone subscribed to that topic on this server gets the message.
Where notifications are published: the public ntfy.sh or your own self-hosted ntfy server.

sections.heading: Have an app subscribed and your settings saved

cards.title: A subscribed ntfy app
cards.text: An ntfy app or web client subscribed to your topic, to receive the notifications.

cards.title: Saved plugin settings
cards.text: Set `server` and `topic` with `/plugin configure ntfy@wovemind`, or the dialog shown when the plugin is enabled.

blocks.caption: Run /ntfy:configure, or ask "set up ntfy on my phone", for a step-by-step walkthrough.

blocks.title: The two plugin settings
rows: The ntfy server every notification is published to. Point it at your own instance if you self-host.
The topic notifications go to unless you name another one in a request.

blocks.text: The defaults only take effect after you save the dialog once. Until then the skill (and the notify-me command) falls back to `https://ntfy.sh` and `claude` itself, except when `~/.ntfy` exists (see stop 6).

blocks.title: Opinionated defaults
rows: the `topic` setting; for one message, name another topic in your request (for example `ci-alerts`), or `-o <topic>` with `ntfy-send`

blocks.title: No environment variables, one optional file
blocks.text: **Auth token** (optional): if `~/.ntfy` exists, its one line, a `tk_...` access token made with `ntfy token add` on the server, is sent as a Bearer token to whatever `server` is configured, including the public ntfy.sh. Public ntfy.sh needs no token.

sections.heading: Treat the topic name like a password

before.label: Easy to guess
before.text: On the public ntfy.sh, anyone who subscribes to a topic name receives its messages, and `claude` is an easy name to guess.

after.label: Safer
after.text: If you use ntfy.sh, set the `topic` setting to a long random name, or run your own server with access control.

blocks.caption: The plan-tools and compliance-audit alerts use the same topic setting too.

sections.heading: A notification can carry far more than a line of text

blocks.title: Common fields
rows: turns on bold, italic, links and code in the message
a URL opened when the notification is tapped

blocks.title: Pick the priority by how much it should interrupt

cards.title: High or urgent plus tag
cards.text: When the message is actionable or time-sensitive: failures, approvals needed.

blocks.caption: It is the difference between a notification that interrupts and one that just logs.

blocks.title: Also possible
items: Attachments: a link to an external file, or a local file uploaded.
Action buttons: open a URL, fire an HTTP request (such as an approve or rollback button), or copy text to the clipboard.
Updating or deleting a message already published.

sections.heading: Know the size, delay and naming limits before you send

items.label: Largest message body
items.note: non-UTF-8 content is treated as an attachment instead

items.label: Largest attachment
items.note: per file, ntfy.sh default; self-hosted may differ

blocks.title: All limits
items: Message body: 4,096 bytes at most. Non-UTF-8 content is treated as an attachment instead of failing outright.
Attachments: 15 MB per file (the ntfy.sh default; a self-hosted server may be set differently). Uploaded files expire after 3 hours on ntfy.sh.
Delayed delivery: from 10 seconds to 3 days ahead.
Action buttons: 3 per notification at most.
Topic names: letters, numbers, underscores and dashes, 64 characters at most.

sections.heading: With a token file, nothing is sent until the server is saved

blocks.title: How the server is chosen
blocks.caption: The token is sent to whatever server is set, so nothing goes out until you choose one.

blocks.text: When it stops, Claude asks you to run `/plugin configure ntfy@wovemind` and save `server`: to your own server, or to `https://ntfy.sh` if that is where the token belongs.

When the skill runs unattended, called from another skill such as plan-tools `drain-issues` or compliance-audit `apply`, it skips the notification and says so in the report instead of stopping that skill.
Do not point `server` at a server you do not trust with the token, or move the file away first.

sections.heading: You can also send a push yourself from the terminal

blocks.title: The ntfy-send command the plugin puts on your PATH
blocks.code:
ntfy-send -s https://ntfy.sh "Build finished" -t "my-repo" -p 4 -o my-topic
ntfy-send --help   # self-check: prints usage and exits 0

blocks.title: What the flags in that example mean
The same kind of push with plain curl
blocks.code:
curl -H "Title: Build failed" \
     -H "Priority: high" \
     -H "Tags: warning,rotating_light" \
     -d "CI pipeline failed on main branch" \
     https://ntfy.sh/ci-alerts

nodes.label: Build failed alert
nodes.note: Title "Build failed", priority high, tags warning and rotating_light.

sections.heading: A printed id means the server accepted it

before.label: Accepted
before.text: A successful send prints a JSON line containing an "id" field. Claude checks for it rather than assuming the notification landed.

after.label: Refused
after.text: `ntfy-send` exits with an error on an HTTP error, such as a bad or expired token or a topic you are not allowed to use.
